comparator.name: Law in Society
comparator.sourceNotes: The English full-time VU Law in Society bachelor, RIO59334, has no formal specialisation (2026–2027 OER7.1/10.2). The complete pathway has ten compulsory6EC units in each of Years1–2, three compulsory6EC Recap units, a12EC thesis and30EC open study:180EC. Recap entry requires36EC from the specified eight substantive legal/theme units. Thesis entry requires Evaluation Research plus at least30EC from the specified legal/theme/Recap units; the annual course clarifies the OER’s run-together PublicLaw/Terrorism line as separate units. All eight substantive units are completed beforeYear3 in this pathway. The thesis combines an individual legal-doctrinal/empirical written study90% with a group empirical component and scientific poster10%; legal analysis/data interpretation remain individual. The English diagnostic or completed refresher gates the Diversity grade. The guide lists zero-credit PPI coaching in allthree years separately from180EC. BSA normally requires42first-yearEC. Required practical attendance and repeat attendance follow course manuals; absence can exclude exam andresit. Open study is a VUminor, approved coherent30ECpackage or facultyexchange; exchange/alternative packages require at least12EClevel300 and at most6EClevel100. University/listed minors have stated approval exemptions but entrance requirements still apply. Civiel Effect is optional additional Dutch legal preparation with separate entry rules and a suitable law master; it is not conferred automatically by this bachelor or any UCR programme. Additional honours are excluded.
components: Public and Private actors in the Platform Economy
Migration Law and the Nation State

core: Law used as an instrument to analyse and address social challenges, integrating public, private and criminal law around societal problems
Human rights, justice and the philosophical/ethical foundations of law
Combining legal analysis with sociological and psychological perspectives on institutions and behaviour
Empirical legal-social research: quantitative statistics and qualitative methods used to evaluate law and design policy
International law, EU law and global governance, including migration governance
Security, terrorism and criminal justice examined through law, philosophy and psychology
Negotiation, mediation and dispute resolution applied to legal-social problems
adjacent: Sustainability, climate and corporate responsibility, including environmental governance and the ethics of AI/technology
Globalisation of markets, the platform economy and worker/consumer protection
questions: How can law and policy evaluation improve responses to global challenges such as migration, security, sustainability and market globalisation?
How should companies and digital platforms be held accountable for environmental harm and for the treatment of workers and consumers?

trace: Case law, trial simulations and legal/social/normative perspectives establish the integrated law-and-society foundation.
Human-rights treaties, monitoring/case law and natural-law philosophy connect legal protection to justice and ethical argument.
Sociological theories and institutions, race/gender and colonial contexts provide a social explanation of the settings in which law operates.
Research design, sampling, operationalisation, inference/ANOVA and a group project supply empirical methods for investigating law-related social questions.
Social influences on judgments, attitudes and behaviour supply the psychological perspective needed to interpret legal actors and public responses.
Competing international-relations explanations and a SecurityCouncilsimulation supply institutional/political perspectives on global legal governance.
Fairness, bias, privacy, responsibility and AI decision-making provide ethical/psychological analysis relevant to legal AI; not VU’s computational methods or legal-application training.
Venture ideation, market validation and business planning explain how firms formulate transactions and commercial models later examined in transnational/platform-business law; not legal doctrine.
Criminal accountability, guilt, legality, punishment and simulated legal advice implement substantive criminal-law reasoning; criminological causation remains limited.
Comparative property, tort and contract principles and their social pressures supply the private-law strand of the legal response.
Climate mechanisms, social effects, justice and mitigation establish the factual background for evaluating legal/governance climate responses; not treaty or corporate climate law.
Cross-border contracts, trade, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce provide substantive transnational business-law analysis.
BATNA/ZOPA, bargaining structures, trade-offs and negotiation simulations provide dispute-negotiation skills; mediation procedure is not assumed.
Public international law, force, international criminal/refugee/environmental law and compliance supply global legal-governance analysis; not a dedicated migration-law sequence.
Comparative constitutional/administrative principles, state power and rights supply public-law reasoning across legal systems.
EU institutions, legislative dossiers and organised-interest research explain the political process through which legal rules and economic policies are formed.
Consumer/firm incentives, market structure and aggregate economic effects explain behaviour of actors regulated in platform/transnational-business settings; not legal protection itself.
Theoretical tools, knowledge, responsibility and rigorous argumentation support reflective legal/normative reasoning; not a dedicated philosophy-of-law course.
Evidence-based youth resilience and participation in an international research project supply a specific prevention/empirical contribution to extremism; not terrorism offences or sanctions law.
Research design, interviews/meaning, data interpretation and reflexivity supply qualitative methods before later applied empirical work.
EU legal institutions, rights, citizenship and free movement analysed through cases/PBL supply the multilevel European-law strand.
Conflict causes, violence, structural inequality and peacebuilding/reconciliation explain social problems addressed by security and justice institutions; not criminal doctrine.
Rule-making, governmental/nonstate actors, interests and sustainability policy/enforcement supply governance analysis complementary to environmental law; not professional legal ethics.

alternatives.label: Law, justice and global governance
alternatives.concept: Substantial study of human-rights, criminal, private, constitutional, international and EU law combines with empirical research, sociology, psychology and negotiation to analyse justice, security and global governance. Climate science, sustainability governance and firm-level foundations provide specific complements. This does not reproduce VU’s dedicated migration, terrorism, platform-worker and climate-law progression, integrated evaluation research, professional-identity trajectory or compulsory thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by doctrinal law (human rights, criminal, private, constitutional, EU and international law) integrated with political science, sociology, psychology, philosophy and negotiation; the combination label describes this multi-field legal/governance programme rather than treating one strand as the whole.
progression: All24actual workbook prerequisites and assigned-term offerings verified. Lawgateway precedes allformal-law continuations; BusinessFoundations precedesTransnationalBusinessLaw; Statistics precedesNegotiation. QualitativeMethods moved fromfinalterm toYear1before the laterempiricalYouthResilienceproject. This is advisoryprogression, not an invented prerequisite. selection.assessment: Retain one substantive law/social-research response. The sustainability/business candidate is genuinely evidenced and coherent, but its two law courses15EC do not establish the defining integrated legal-doctrinal/empirical approach. General economics, marketing, materials science and historical empire study cannot stand in for corporate environmental liability, platform-worker/public-law protection or legal-policy evaluation. Broad environmental/business coherence alone is insufficient under CP119. Preserve that proposal as reviewed evidence, not an included alternative. Relevant sustainability/global-market interests have specific complementary treatment in the retained law programme; no third alternative is manufactured.

notes.text: UCR combines substantial public, private, criminal, international and human-rights law with social and empirical methods. It does not reproduce VU’s dedicated migration, terrorism, platform-worker and climate-law sequence, integrated legal-policy evaluation, PPI trajectory or compulsory legal/empirical thesis. UCR climate science and youth resilience are factual/prevention complements. The programme does not confer a Dutch legal qualification or automatic postgraduate eligibility.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Law in Society integrates public, private and criminal law with social sciences and empirical inquiry. Security, migration, sustainability and global markets organise study of how legal approaches address societal problems.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One qualified UCR alternative combines substantial study across legal fields with sociology, psychology, qualitative and quantitative methods, negotiation and global governance. It provides a substantive legal and social-science response while leaving specialist migration, terrorism, platform-worker and climate law, integrated evaluation research and VU’s compulsory thesis explicit as gaps.

curriculum.limitation: The complete pathway contains 180 EC, including 30 EC open study and a 12 EC thesis combining legal and empirical research. Thesis entry requires Evaluation Research and at least 30 EC from specified legal/theme units; the Recap courses require 36 EC from eight specified units. The English diagnostic or refresher gates Diversity. PPI coaching in all three years carries no credits. Additional Dutch Civiel Effect preparation and a suitable law master are separate conditions for professional legal routes.
